title: Appointments & Plans
subtitle: Book, move and organise your appointments in French

lessons.title: Prendre rendez-vous
lessons.description: Book an appointment with a doctor, a hairdresser or an office, by phone and online.

blocks.heading: Asking for an appointment
blocks.body: The key phrase is prendre rendez-vous — literally "to take an appointment". You use it with avec (with a person) or chez (at a professional's place). To ask for one on the phone, start politely with Je voudrais or J'aimerais, which sound much softer than Je veux.

examples.french: Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous, s'il vous plaît.
examples.english: I would like to make an appointment, please.
examples.note: The standard opening line on the phone.

examples.french: J'aimerais un rendez-vous avec le docteur Morel.
examples.english: I would like an appointment with Doctor Morel.

examples.french: Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous chez le dentiste.
examples.english: I would like to make an appointment at the dentist's.

examples.french: C'est pour une consultation, pas pour une urgence.
examples.english: It's for a consultation, not for an emergency.

examples.french: Est-ce que vous avez de la place cette semaine ?
examples.english: Do you have any room this week?

blocks.tip: Say bonjour before anything else. In France, jumping straight to your request without greeting sounds rude.

blocks.heading: Talking about time slots
blocks.body: A free time is un créneau (a slot). The secretary will offer you slots and ask if they suit you. Answer with Ça me convient (that suits me) or Ce n'est pas possible pour moi (that isn't possible for me). Days and times come after à or le.

examples.french: J'ai un créneau mardi à 14 h 30.
examples.english: I have a slot on Tuesday at 2:30 p.m.

examples.french: Est-ce que vous êtes disponible jeudi matin ?
examples.english: Are you available on Thursday morning?

examples.french: Oui, jeudi matin, ça me convient très bien.
examples.english: Yes, Thursday morning suits me very well.

examples.french: Désolé, je ne suis pas libre avant 17 h.
examples.english: Sorry, I'm not free before 5 p.m.

examples.french: Vous avez quelque chose plus tôt dans la semaine ?
examples.english: Do you have anything earlier in the week?

blocks.tip: French official times use the 24-hour clock: 14 h 30, 17 h 45. In speech, quatorze heures trente.

blocks.heading: On the phone and online
blocks.body: On the phone you will hear Allô ?, Ne quittez pas (hold the line) and Je vous mets en attente. Online you fill in un formulaire, choose un créneau and confirm. Booking sites usually send you une confirmation by email or SMS.

examples.french: Allô, bonjour, cabinet du docteur Lambert.
examples.english: Hello, good morning, Doctor Lambert's surgery.

examples.french: Ne quittez pas, je regarde l'agenda.
examples.english: Hold the line, I'm looking at the diary.

blocks.heading: chez + person, à + place
blocks.body: Use chez before a person or a profession: chez le médecin, chez le coiffeur, chez le dentiste. Use à + le → au before a place or a building: au cabinet, au salon, à la clinique. Remember the contractions: à + le = au, à + les = aux.

blocks.tip: Chez never changes: chez le, chez la, chez les — no contraction.

blocks.heading: Asking politely: est-ce que and inversion
blocks.body: There are three ways to ask a question. Rising intonation is casual (Vous avez un créneau ?), est-ce que is neutral and safe (Est-ce que vous avez un créneau ?), and inversion is the most formal (Avez-vous un créneau ?). On the phone with a stranger, est-ce que or inversion is the right choice.

passages.title: Un appel au cabinet médical
passages.french:
— Allô, bonjour, cabinet du docteur Lambert, j'écoute.
— Bonjour madame. Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous, s'il vous plaît.
— Bien sûr. C'est pour quel motif ?
— C'est pour une consultation simple, ce n'est pas urgent.
— Très bien. Ne quittez pas, je regarde les disponibilités... Le docteur a un créneau mardi à 11 h 15.
— Mardi matin, ce n'est pas possible pour moi, je travaille.
— Alors jeudi à 17 h 45 ?
— Jeudi à 17 h 45, ça me convient très bien.
— Parfait. Vous recevrez une confirmation par SMS. N'oubliez pas votre carte Vitale.
— Merci beaucoup, bonne journée !
passages.english:
— Hello, good morning, Doctor Lambert's surgery, how can I help?
— Good morning. I would like to make an appointment, please.
— Of course. What is it for?
— It's for an ordinary consultation, it isn't urgent.
— Very good. Hold the line, I'm looking at the availability... The doctor has a slot on Tuesday at 11:15 a.m.
— Tuesday morning isn't possible for me, I'm working.
— Then Thursday at 5:45 p.m.?
— Thursday at 5:45 p.m. suits me very well.
— Perfect. You will receive a confirmation by text message. Don't forget your health card.
— Thank you very much, have a good day!

lessons.title: Changer un rendez-vous
lessons.description: Postpone or cancel an appointment politely using the conditional.

blocks.heading: Moving an appointment
blocks.body: Three verbs do most of the work: reporter (to postpone to a later date), déplacer (to move to another slot) and décaler (to shift by a short time). Their opposite is avancer, to bring forward. All of them take the appointment as the object: reporter mon rendez-vous.

examples.french: Je voudrais reporter mon rendez-vous à la semaine prochaine.
examples.english: I would like to postpone my appointment to next week.

examples.french: Pouvez-vous déplacer le rendez-vous à jeudi ?
examples.english: Can you move the appointment to Thursday?

examples.french: On peut décaler d'une demi-heure ?
examples.english: Can we shift it by half an hour?

examples.french: J'aimerais avancer le rendez-vous à 9 h.
examples.english: I would like to bring the appointment forward to 9 a.m.

examples.french: Je dois changer l'heure de ma consultation.
examples.english: I have to change the time of my consultation.

blocks.tip: Décaler is for small shifts (fifteen minutes, an hour); reporter is for another day.

blocks.heading: Cancelling and apologising
blocks.body: To cancel is annuler and the noun is l'annulation. Cancelling politely means giving a reason and apologising: Je suis désolé(e), j'ai un empêchement. French callers almost always add a reason — un imprévu, une réunion, un problème de transport.

examples.french: Je suis désolée, je dois annuler mon rendez-vous.
examples.english: I'm sorry, I have to cancel my appointment.

examples.french: J'ai un empêchement de dernière minute.
examples.english: Something has come up at the last minute.

examples.french: Excusez-moi de prévenir si tard.
examples.english: I'm sorry for letting you know so late.

examples.french: Malheureusement, je ne pourrai pas venir mardi.
examples.english: Unfortunately, I won't be able to come on Tuesday.

examples.french: Je vous rappelle demain pour reprendre rendez-vous.
examples.english: I'll call you back tomorrow to book again.

blocks.tip: Most French practices ask you to cancel at least 24 hours ahead, or you may be charged.

blocks.heading: Being late
blocks.body: If you are running late, say je vais avoir un peu de retard or je serai en retard. If you arrive early, you are en avance; on time is à l'heure. To miss the appointment completely is rater or manquer son rendez-vous.

examples.english: I'm going to be ten minutes late, sorry.

examples.french: Le train a du retard, je serai en retard.

examples.french: Si vous manquez le rendez-vous, prévenez-nous.
examples.english: If you miss the appointment, let us know.

blocks.tip: Prévenir means to let someone know in advance — a very common French verb in this situation.

blocks.heading: The polite conditional (le conditionnel de politesse)
blocks.body: To sound polite, French uses the conditional instead of the present. Build it from the future stem plus the imparfait endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. The three you need most are je voudrais (vouloir), je pourrais / vous pourriez (pouvoir) and ce serait (être).

examples.french: Je voudrais reporter mon rendez-vous.
examples.english: I would like to postpone my appointment.

examples.french: Pourriez-vous me rappeler cet après-midi ?
examples.english: Could you call me back this afternoon?

blocks.tip: In a shop, surgery or office, je voudrais is almost always the right choice; je veux sounds blunt.

blocks.heading: Saying why: parce que, à cause de, donc
blocks.body: When you change an appointment, you explain why. Parce que introduces a whole clause (parce que je travaille). À cause de introduces a noun (à cause d'une réunion). Donc introduces the consequence: donc je dois annuler.

examples.french: Je dois annuler parce que je suis malade.
examples.english: I have to cancel because I'm ill.

examples.french: Je serai en retard à cause des travaux.

examples.french: Mon train est annulé, donc je vais décaler.
examples.english: My train is cancelled, so I'm going to shift the time.

blocks.tip: À cause de suggests a negative cause; for a positive one, French says grâce à (thanks to).

passages.french:
Chère Madame Bertin,
Je vous écris au sujet de notre rendez-vous de mercredi 14 h.
Malheureusement, j'ai un empêchement : mon chef a fixé une réunion importante au même moment.

lessons.title: Mon agenda
lessons.description: Plan a whole week with the futur proche, days, times and availability.

blocks.heading: Talking about your week
blocks.body: Your diary is un agenda (never "un journal", which is a newspaper). A work schedule is un emploi du temps or un planning. To say what you have on, use avoir + activity or être pris(e), meaning to be tied up.

examples.french: Mon agenda est très chargé cette semaine.
examples.english: My diary is very full this week.

examples.french: J'ai une réunion lundi et un cours mercredi.
examples.english: I have a meeting on Monday and a class on Wednesday.

examples.french: Je suis prise toute la journée de jeudi.
examples.english: I'm tied up all day on Thursday.

examples.french: Mon emploi du temps change chaque semaine.
examples.english: My schedule changes every week.

examples.french: Vendredi, je n'ai rien de prévu.
examples.english: On Friday I have nothing planned.

blocks.tip: Rien de prévu (nothing planned) is the natural way to say a day is empty.

blocks.heading: Days: lundi or le lundi ?
blocks.body: Lundi on its own means next Monday, one specific day. Le lundi means every Monday, a habit. Days are never capitalised in French, and you do not add a preposition: not "à lundi matin" but lundi matin.

examples.french: Lundi, je vais chez le dentiste.
examples.english: On Monday I'm going to the dentist.

examples.french: Le lundi, je travaille à la maison.
examples.english: On Mondays I work from home.

examples.french: Mardi matin, j'ai un rendez-vous à 9 h.
examples.english: On Tuesday morning I have an appointment at 9 a.m.

examples.french: Le samedi, le salon ferme à 17 h.
examples.english: On Saturdays the salon closes at 5 p.m.

examples.french: On se voit dimanche après-midi ?
examples.english: Shall we meet on Sunday afternoon?

blocks.tip: Matin, après-midi and soir simply follow the day: jeudi soir, samedi matin.

blocks.heading: Saying when, exactly
blocks.body: Use de... à for a period (de 9 h à 11 h), vers for approximately (vers midi), avant and après for before and after. Une demi-heure is half an hour and un quart d'heure is a quarter of an hour.

examples.french: Je suis en réunion de 9 h à 11 h.
examples.english: I'm in a meeting from 9 to 11 a.m.

examples.french: On se retrouve vers midi et demi ?
examples.english: Shall we meet around half past twelve?

examples.french: Je serai libre après 16 h.
examples.english: I'll be free after 4 p.m.

examples.french: La pause dure un quart d'heure.
examples.english: The break lasts a quarter of an hour.

examples.french: Il me faut une demi-heure pour y aller.
examples.english: It takes me half an hour to get there.

blocks.tip: Vers means "around" for time; environ is used more for quantities and durations.

blocks.heading: Le futur proche: aller + infinitive
blocks.body: For plans, French uses aller in the present plus an infinitive: je vais, tu vas, il/elle va, nous allons, vous allez, ils/elles vont. To make it negative, put ne... pas around the form of aller: je ne vais pas travailler. Pronouns go in front of the infinitive: je vais les appeler.

examples.french: Lundi, je vais prendre rendez-vous chez le dentiste.
examples.english: On Monday I'm going to make an appointment at the dentist's.

examples.french: Nous allons organiser la réunion jeudi.
examples.english: We're going to organise the meeting on Thursday.

examples.french: Elle va appeler le salon cet après-midi.
examples.english: She's going to call the salon this afternoon.

examples.english: I'm not going to work on Friday.

examples.french: Ils vont te prévenir la veille.
examples.english: They're going to let you know the day before.

blocks.tip: Use the futur proche for anything already decided; it is far more common in speech than the simple future.

blocks.heading: Time expressions: dans, en, pendant, jusqu'à
blocks.body: Dans says how long before something starts (dans deux jours = in two days' time). En says how long an action takes (en dix minutes). Pendant covers a duration (pendant une heure) and jusqu'à means until a point in time.

examples.french: Mon rendez-vous est dans trois jours.
examples.english: My appointment is in three days' time.

examples.french: J'ai rempli le formulaire en cinq minutes.

examples.french: Le cabinet est ouvert jusqu'à 19 h.
examples.english: The surgery is open until 7 p.m.

examples.french: Je suis en réunion jusqu'à midi.
examples.english: I'm in a meeting until midday.

blocks.tip: Dans looks forward from now; il y a looks back: il y a deux jours means two days ago.

passages.title: La semaine de Camille
passages.french:
Cette semaine, l'agenda de Camille est très chargé.
Lundi matin, elle va au bureau pour une réunion de 9 h à 11 h.
Mardi, elle a un rendez-vous chez le dentiste à 14 h 30 ; elle va partir plus tôt du travail.
Le mercredi, elle ne travaille jamais l'après-midi : c'est le jour des enfants.
Jeudi, elle va enfin prendre rendez-vous chez le coiffeur, parce qu'elle attend depuis un mois.
Vendredi, sa journée est libre, mais elle va sûrement rattraper son retard.
Samedi matin, il y a l'entraînement de foot de son fils à 10 h.
Dimanche, elle ne prévoit rien du tout : elle va se reposer.
Le dimanche soir, elle regarde toujours son planning de la semaine suivante.
Elle note ses rendez-vous dans son agenda et sur son téléphone.
passages.english:
This week, Camille's diary is very full.
On Monday morning she goes to the office for a meeting from 9 to 11.
On Tuesday she has a dentist's appointment at 2:30 p.m.; she's going to leave work earlier.
On Wednesdays she never works in the afternoon: it's the children's day.
On Thursday she's finally going to make an appointment at the hairdresser's, because she has been waiting for a month.
On Friday her day is free, but she will surely catch up on her backlog.
On Saturday morning there is her son's football training at 10 a.m.
On Sunday she is planning nothing at all: she's going to rest.
On Sunday evenings she always looks at her schedule for the following week.
She writes her appointments in her diary and on her phone.
